passages.text: Now when the queen of Sheba heard about the fame of Solomon, she came to test him with difficult questions. She arrived in Jerusalem with a very large caravan—with camels bearing spices, gold in abundance, and precious stones. So she came to Solomon and spoke with him about all that was on her mind.
passages.sermon:
The queen of Sheba was a powerful and wealthy ruler.
She heard about the fame of King Solomon.
She wanted to test Solomon with difficult questions.
She traveled to Jerusalem.
She brought a very large caravan with her.
Her camels carried many spices.
Her camels also carried much gold.
Her camels carried precious stones.
She came to Solomon.
She spoke with Solomon about everything on her mind.
passages.original: וּמַֽלְכַּת־ שְׁבָ֗א שָֽׁמְעָה֮ אֶת־ שֵׁ֣מַע שְׁלֹמֹה֒ וַתָּב֣וֹא לְנַסּוֹת֩ אֶת־ שְׁלֹמֹ֨ה בְחִיד֜וֹת בִּירֽוּשָׁלִַ֗ם בְּחַ֣יִל כָּבֵ֣ד מְאֹ֡ד וּ֠גְמַלִּים נֹשְׂאִ֨ים בְּשָׂמִ֧ים וְזָהָ֛ב לָרֹ֖ב וְאֶ֣בֶן יְקָרָ֑ה וַתָּבוֹא֙ אֶל־ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה וַתְּדַבֵּ֣ר עִמּ֔וֹ אֵ֛ת כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָיָ֖ה עִם־ לְבָבָֽהּ׃

passages.text: And Solomon answered all her questions; nothing was too difficult for him to explain.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon was wise.
The queen of Sheba asked Solomon many questions.
Solomon answered every question she asked.
He explained everything to her.
Nothing was hidden from Solomon.
He told her everything she wanted to know.
passages.original: וַיַּגֶּד־ לָ֥הּ שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה אֶת־ כָּל־ דְּבָרֶ֑יהָ וְלֹֽא־ נֶעְלַ֤ם דָּבָר֙ מִשְּׁלֹמֹ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֧ר לֹ֦א הִגִּ֖יד לָֽהּ׃

passages.text: When the queen of Sheba saw the wisdom of Solomon, the palace he had built, the food at his table, the seating of his servants, the service and attire of his attendants and cupbearers, and the burnt offerings he presented at the house of the LORD, it took her breath away.
passages.sermon:
The queen of Sheba visited Solomon in Jerusalem.
She saw Solomon’s wisdom.
She saw the palace Solomon had built.
She saw the food on Solomon’s table.
She saw where Solomon’s servants sat.
She saw how Solomon’s attendants stood ready to serve.
She saw the clothes of Solomon’s attendants.
She saw the cupbearers and their clothing.
She saw the burnt offerings Solomon brought up to the house of the LORD.
All these things amazed the queen of Sheba.
She was left without breath.
passages.original: וַתֵּ֙רֶא֙ מַֽלְכַּת־ שְׁבָ֔א אֵ֖ת חָכְמַ֣ת שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה וְהַבַּ֖יִת אֲשֶׁ֥ר בָּנָֽה׃ וּמַאֲכַ֣ל שֻׁלְחָנ֡וֹ וּמוֹשַׁ֣ב עֲבָדָיו֩ וּמַעֲמַ֨ד מְשָׁרְתָ֜יו וּמַלְבּֽוּשֵׁיהֶ֗ם וּמַשְׁקָיו֙ וּמַלְבּ֣וּשֵׁיהֶ֔ם וַעֲלִיָּת֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר יַעֲלֶ֖ה בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה וְלֹא־ הָ֥יָה ע֛וֹד בָּ֖הּ רֽוּחַ׃

passages.text: She said to the king, “The report I heard in my own country about your words and wisdom is true.
passages.sermon:
The queen of Sheba spoke to King Solomon.
She said, "The report I heard in my own country is true.
I heard about your words.
I heard about your wisdom.
What I heard is true."
passages.original: וַתֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֱמֶת֙ הַדָּבָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁמַ֖עְתִּי בְּאַרְצִ֑י עַל־ דְּבָרֶ֖יךָ וְעַל־ חָכְמָתֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: But I did not believe the reports until I came and saw with my own eyes. Indeed, not half of the greatness of your wisdom was told to me. You have far exceeded the report I heard.
passages.sermon:
The queen of Sheba spoke to King Solomon.
She said she did not believe the reports about him.
She did not trust what people said about his wisdom.
She came to Jerusalem to see for herself.
She saw everything with her own eyes.
She realized the reports did not tell her even half of the truth.
His wisdom was much greater than she had heard.
He had far exceeded everything she was told.
passages.original: וְלֹֽא־ הֶאֱמַ֣נְתִּי לְדִבְרֵיהֶ֗ם עַ֤ד אֲשֶׁר־ בָּ֙אתִי֙ וַתִּרְאֶ֣ינָה עֵינַ֔י וְהִנֵּה֙ לֹ֣א הֻגַּד־ לִ֔י חֲצִ֖י מַרְבִּ֣ית חָכְמָתֶ֑ךָ יָסַ֕פְתָּ עַל־ הַשְּׁמוּעָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁמָֽעְתִּי׃

passages.text: How blessed are your men! How blessed are these servants of yours who stand continually before you and hear your wisdom!
passages.sermon:
King Solomon was wise.
He had many men.
He had many servants.
Your men are blessed.
Your servants are blessed.
These servants stand before you all the time.
They hear your wisdom.
passages.original: אַשְׁרֵ֣י אֲנָשֶׁ֔יךָ וְאַשְׁרֵ֖י עֲבָדֶ֣יךָ אֵ֑לֶּה הָעֹמְדִ֤ים לְפָנֶ֙יךָ֙ תָּמִ֔יד וְשֹׁמְעִ֖ים אֶת־ חָכְמָתֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: Blessed be the LORD your God, who has delighted in you to set you on His throne to be king for the LORD your God. Because your God loved Israel enough to establish them forever, He has made you king over them to carry out justice and righteousness.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD is your God.
The LORD deserves blessing.
The LORD delighted in you.
The LORD set you on His throne.
The LORD made you king.
You are king for the LORD your God.
God loves Israel.
God wants Israel to stand forever.
God made you king over Israel.
You must do justice.
You must do righteousness.
passages.original: יְהִ֨י יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֙יךָ֙ בָּר֔וּךְ אֲשֶׁ֣ר׀ חָפֵ֣ץ בְּךָ֗ לְתִתְּךָ֤ עַל־ כִּסְאוֹ֙ לְמֶ֔לֶךְ לַיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ בְּאַהֲבַ֨ת אֱלֹהֶ֤יךָ אֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לְהַעֲמִיד֣וֹ לְעוֹלָ֔ם וַיִּתֶּנְךָ֤ עֲלֵיהֶם֙ לְמֶ֔לֶךְ לַעֲשׂ֖וֹת מִשְׁפָּ֥ט וּצְדָקָֽה׃

passages.text: Then she gave the king 120 talents of gold, a great quantity of spices, and precious stones. There had never been such spices as those the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon.
passages.sermon:
The queen of Sheba visited King Solomon.
She gave King Solomon 120 talents of gold.
She gave him a very large amount of spices.
She also gave him precious stones.
No one had ever given spices like those before.
The spices the queen of Sheba gave to King Solomon were unique.
passages.original: וַתִּתֵּ֨ן לַמֶּ֜לֶךְ מֵאָ֥ה וְעֶשְׂרִ֣ים׀ כִּכַּ֣ר זָהָ֗ב וּבְשָׂמִ֛ים לָרֹ֥ב מְאֹ֖ד וְאֶ֣בֶן יְקָרָ֑ה וְלֹ֤א הָיָה֙ כַּבֹּ֣שֶׂם הַה֔וּא אֲשֶׁר־ נָתְנָ֥ה מַֽלְכַּת־ שְׁבָ֖א לַמֶּ֥לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹֽה׃

passages.text: (The servants of Hiram and of Solomon who brought gold from Ophir also brought algum wood and precious stones.
passages.sermon:
The servants of Hiram and the servants of Solomon worked together.
They brought gold from Ophir.
They also brought algum wood.
They brought precious stones.
passages.original: וְגַם־ עַבְדֵ֤י חִירָם וְעַבְדֵ֣י שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־ הֵבִ֥יאוּ זָהָ֖ב מֵאוֹפִ֑יר הֵבִ֛יאוּ עֲצֵ֥י אַלְגּוּמִּ֖ים וְאֶ֥בֶן יְקָרָֽה׃

passages.text: The king made the algum wood into steps for the house of the LORD and for the king’s palace, and into lyres and harps for the singers. Never before had anything like them been seen in the land of Judah.)
passages.sermon:
King Solomon was the ruler of Israel.
He took algum wood.
He made steps for the house of the LORD from this wood.
He also made steps for his own palace from this wood.
He made lyres from the algum wood.
He made harps for the singers from the algum wood.
No one had ever seen such things before in the land of Judah.
passages.original: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ הַ֠מֶּלֶךְ אֶת־ עֲצֵ֨י הָֽאַלְגּוּמִּ֜ים מְסִלּ֤וֹת לְבֵית־ יְהוָה֙ וּלְבֵ֣ית הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְכִנֹּר֥וֹת וּנְבָלִ֖ים לַשָּׁרִ֑ים וְלֹא־ נִרְא֥וּ כָהֵ֛ם לְפָנִ֖ים בְּאֶ֥רֶץ יְהוּדָֽה׃

passages.text: King Solomon gave the queen of Sheba all she desired—whatever she asked—far more than she had brought the king. Then she left and returned to her own country, along with her servants.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon was the king of Israel.
The queen of Sheba visited King Solomon.
She asked King Solomon for many things.
King Solomon gave the queen of Sheba everything she wanted.
He gave her all that she asked for.
He gave her more than she had brought to him.
After this, the queen of Sheba left King Solomon.
She returned to her own country.
Her servants went with her.
passages.original: וְהַמֶּ֨לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֜ה נָתַ֣ן לְמַֽלְכַּת־ שְׁבָ֗א אֶת־ כָּל־ חֶפְצָהּ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁאָ֔לָה מִלְּבַ֖ד אֲשֶׁר־ הֵבִ֣יאָה אֶל־ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַֽתַּהֲפֹ֛ךְ וַתֵּ֥לֶךְ לְאַרְצָ֖הּ הִ֥יא וַעֲבָדֶֽיהָ׃פ

passages.text: The weight of gold that came to Solomon each year was 666 talents, not including the revenue from the merchants and traders. And all the Arabian kings and governors of the land also brought gold and silver to Solomon.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon ruled Israel.
Each year, Solomon received much gold.
The gold weighed 666 talents every year.
This amount did not include gold from merchants.
This amount did not include gold from traders.
All the kings of Arabia brought gold to Solomon.
All the governors of the land brought gold to Solomon.
They also brought silver to Solomon.
passages.original: וַיְהִי֙ מִשְׁקַ֣ל הַזָּהָ֔ב אֲשֶׁר־ בָּ֥א לִשְׁלֹמֹ֖ה בְּשָׁנָ֣ה אֶחָ֑ת שֵׁ֥שׁ מֵא֛וֹת וְשִׁשִּׁ֥ים וָשֵׁ֖שׁ כִּכְּרֵ֥י זָהָֽב׃ לְבַ֞ד מֵאַנְשֵׁ֧י הַתָּרִ֛ים וְהַסֹּחֲרִ֖ים מְבִיאִ֑ים וְכָל־ מַלְכֵ֤י עֲרַב֙ וּפַח֣וֹת הָאָ֔רֶץ מְבִיאִ֛ים זָהָ֥ב וָכֶ֖סֶף לִשְׁלֹמֹֽה׃

passages.text: King Solomon made two hundred large shields of hammered gold; six hundred shekels of hammered gold went into each shield.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon was the king of Israel.
King Solomon made two hundred large shields.
He used hammered gold to make these shields.
Each shield contained six hundred shekels of hammered gold.
passages.original: וַיַּ֨עַשׂ הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֛ה מָאתַ֥יִם צִנָּ֖ה זָהָ֣ב שָׁח֑וּט שֵׁ֤שׁ מֵאוֹת֙ זָהָ֣ב שָׁח֔וּט יַעֲלֶ֖ה עַל־ הַצִּנָּ֥ה הָאֶחָֽת׃

passages.text: He also made three hundred small shields of hammered gold; three hundred shekels of gold went into each shield. And the king put them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon ruled Israel.
\r\nHe made three hundred small shields.
\r\nHe used hammered gold to make these shields.
\r\nEach shield contained three hundred shekels of gold.
\r\nKing Solomon placed these shields in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.
passages.original: וּשְׁלֹשׁ־ מֵא֤וֹת מָֽגִנִּים֙ זָהָ֣ב שָׁח֔וּט שְׁלֹ֤שׁ מֵאוֹת֙ זָהָ֔ב יַעֲלֶ֖ה עַל־ הַמָּגֵ֣ן הָאֶחָ֑ת וַיִּתְּנֵ֣ם הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ בְּבֵ֖ית יַ֥עַר הַלְּבָנֽוֹן׃פ

passages.text: Additionally, the king made a great throne of ivory and overlaid it with pure gold.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon was the king of Israel.
King Solomon made a great throne.
He made the throne from ivory.
He covered the throne with pure gold.
passages.original: וַיַּ֧עַשׂ הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ כִּסֵּא־ שֵׁ֖ן גָּד֑וֹל וַיְצַפֵּ֖הוּ זָהָ֥ב טָהֽוֹר׃

passages.text: The throne had six steps, and a footstool of gold was attached to it. There were armrests on both sides of the seat, with a lion standing beside each armrest.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon made a throne.
The throne had six steps.
A footstool of gold was attached to the throne.
The throne had armrests on both sides of the seat.
A lion stood beside each armrest.
passages.original: וְשֵׁ֣שׁ מַעֲל֣וֹת לַ֠כִּסֵּא וְכֶ֨בֶשׁ בַּזָּהָ֤ב לַכִּסֵּא֙ מָאֳחָזִ֔ים וְיָד֛וֹת מִזֶּ֥ה וּמִזֶּ֖ה עַל־ מְק֣וֹם הַשָּׁ֑בֶת וּשְׁנַ֣יִם אֲרָי֔וֹת עֹמְדִ֖ים אֵ֥צֶל הַיָּדֽוֹת׃

passages.text: Twelve lions stood on the six steps, one at either end of each step. Nothing like this had ever been made for any kingdom.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon made a throne with six steps.
He placed twelve lions on the steps.
There was one lion at each end of every step.
No other kingdom had ever made anything like this.
passages.original: וּשְׁנֵ֧ים עָשָׂ֣ר אֲרָי֗וֹת עֹמְדִ֥ים שָׁ֛ם עַל־ שֵׁ֥שׁ הַֽמַּעֲל֖וֹת מִזֶּ֣ה וּמִזֶּ֑ה לֹא־ נַעֲשָׂ֥ה כֵ֖ן לְכָל־ מַמְלָכָֽה׃

passages.text: All King Solomon’s drinking cups were gold, and all the utensils of the House of the Forest of Lebanon were pure gold. There was no silver, because it was accounted as nothing in the days of Solomon.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon ruled Israel.
\r\nHe was famous for his wealth and wisdom.
\r\nAll of King Solomon’s drinking cups were gold.
\r\nAll the utensils in the House of the Forest of Lebanon were pure gold.
\r\nNo one used silver for these items.
\r\nPeople did not value silver during Solomon’s days.
\r\nThey considered silver to be worth nothing.
passages.original: וְ֠כֹל כְּלֵ֞י מַשְׁקֵ֨ה הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה֙ זָהָ֔ב וְכֹ֗ל כְּלֵ֛י בֵּֽית־ יַ֥עַר הַלְּבָנ֖וֹן זָהָ֣ב סָג֑וּר אֵ֣ין כֶּ֗סֶף נֶחְשָׁ֛ב בִּימֵ֥י שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה לִמְאֽוּמָה׃

passages.text: For the king had the ships of Tarshish that went with Hiram’s servants, and once every three years the ships of Tarshish would arrive bearing gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon ruled Israel.
King Solomon was very wealthy and wise.
King Solomon had ships called the ships of Tarshish.
These ships belonged to King Solomon.
The ships traveled with the servants of Hiram.
Hiram was the king of Tyre and an ally of Solomon.
The ships of Tarshish made a journey every three years.
After three years, the ships returned.
The ships brought gold.
The ships brought silver.
The ships brought ivory.
The ships brought apes.
The ships brought peacocks.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ אֳנִיּ֤וֹת לַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ הֹלְכ֣וֹת תַּרְשִׁ֔ישׁ עִ֖ם עַבְדֵ֣י חוּרָ֑ם אַחַת֩ לְשָׁל֨וֹשׁ שָׁנִ֜ים תָּב֣וֹאנָה׀ אֳנִיּ֣וֹת תַּרְשִׁ֗ישׁ נֹֽשְׂאוֹת֙ זָהָ֣ב וָכֶ֔סֶף שֶׁנְהַבִּ֥ים וְקוֹפִ֖ים וְתוּכִּיִּֽים׃פ

passages.text: So King Solomon surpassed all the kings of the earth in riches and wisdom.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon was a king of Israel.
King Solomon became greater than all other kings on earth.
King Solomon had more riches than any other king.
King Solomon had more wisdom than any other king.
passages.original: וַיִּגְדַּל֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה מִכֹּ֖ל מַלְכֵ֣י הָאָ֑רֶץ לְעֹ֖שֶׁר וְחָכְמָֽה׃

passages.text: All the kings of the earth sought an audience with Solomon to hear the wisdom that God had put in his heart.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon ruled Israel.
\r\nGod gave Solomon great wisdom.
\r\nAll the kings of the earth wanted to meet Solomon.
\r\nThey came to hear the wisdom that God placed in Solomon’s heart.
passages.original: וְכֹל֙ מַלְכֵ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ מְבַקְשִׁ֖ים אֶת־ פְּנֵ֣י שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה לִשְׁמֹ֙עַ֙ אֶת־ חָכְמָת֔וֹ אֲשֶׁר־ נָתַ֥ן הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים בְּלִבּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Year after year, each visitor would bring his tribute: articles of silver and gold, clothing, weapons, spices, horses, and mules.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon was greater than all other kings in riches and wisdom.
Every year, visitors came to see Solomon.
Each visitor brought a gift to Solomon.
They brought silver objects.
They brought gold objects.
They brought clothing.
They brought weapons.
They brought spices.
They brought horses.
They brought mules.
They did this every year.
passages.original: וְהֵ֣ם מְבִיאִ֣ים אִ֣ישׁ מִנְחָת֡וֹ כְּלֵ֣י כֶסֶף֩ וּכְלֵ֨י זָהָ֤ב וּשְׂלָמוֹת֙ נֵ֣שֶׁק וּבְשָׂמִ֔ים סוּסִ֖ים וּפְרָדִ֑ים דְּבַר־ שָׁנָ֖ה בְּשָׁנָֽה׃פ

passages.text: Solomon had 4,000 stalls for horses and chariots, and 12,000 horses, which he stationed in the chariot cities and also with him in Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
Solomon was king in Jerusalem.
Solomon had 4,000 stalls for horses and chariots.
Solomon had 12,000 horses.
He placed the horses and chariots in the chariot cities.
He also kept some horses and chariots with him in Jerusalem.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֨י לִשְׁלֹמֹ֜ה אַרְבַּעַת֩ אֲלָפִ֨ים אֻֽרְי֤וֹת סוּסִים֙ וּמַרְכָּב֔וֹת וּשְׁנֵים־ עָשָׂ֥ר אֶ֖לֶף פָּרָשִׁ֑ים וַיַּנִּיחֵם֙ בְּעָרֵ֣י הָרֶ֔כֶב וְעִם־ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

passages.text: He reigned over all the kings from the Euphrates to the land of the Philistines, as far as the border of Egypt.
passages.sermon:
Solomon was king.
He ruled over many other kings.
His rule stretched from the Euphrates River.
It reached to the land of the Philistines.
It went as far as the border of Egypt.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֥י מוֹשֵׁ֖ל בְּכָל־ הַמְּלָכִ֑ים מִן־ הַנָּהָר֙ וְעַד־ אֶ֣רֶץ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וְעַ֖ד גְּב֥וּל מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: The king made silver as common in Jerusalem as stones, and cedar as abundant as sycamore in the foothills.
passages.sermon:
King Solomon ruled in Jerusalem.
He ruled over all Israel.
He made silver very common in Jerusalem.
Silver became as plentiful as stones.
He also brought in much cedar wood.
Cedar became as abundant as sycamore trees in the foothills.
passages.original: וַיִּתֵּ֨ן הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ אֶת־ הַכֶּ֛סֶף בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֖ם כָּאֲבָנִ֑ים וְאֵ֣ת הָאֲרָזִ֗ים נָתַ֛ן כַּשִּׁקְמִ֥ים אֲשֶׁר־ בַּשְּׁפֵלָ֖ה לָרֹֽב׃

passages.text: Solomon’s horses were imported from Egypt and from all the lands.
passages.sermon:
Solomon was king over all Israel.
People brought horses to Solomon.
They brought horses from Egypt.
They also brought horses from every land.
passages.original: וּמוֹצִיאִ֨ים סוּסִ֧ים מִמִּצְרַ֛יִם לִשְׁלֹמֹ֖ה וּמִכָּל־ הָאֲרָצֽוֹת׃

passages.text: As for the rest of the acts of Solomon, from beginning to end, are they not written in the Records of Nathan the Prophet, in the Prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite, and in the Visions of Iddo the Seer concerning Jeroboam son of Nebat?
passages.sermon:
Solomon was king over all Israel.
Solomon did many things from the beginning to the end of his reign.
Writers recorded the rest of Solomon’s acts.
Nathan the Prophet wrote about Solomon’s acts.
Ahijah the Shilonite gave prophecies about Solomon.
Iddo the Seer had visions about Jeroboam son of Nebat.
These records, prophecies, and visions include the rest of Solomon’s acts.
passages.original: וּשְׁאָר֙ דִּבְרֵ֣י שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה הָרִאשֹׁנִ֖ים וְהָאֲחֲרוֹנִ֑ים הֲלֹא־ הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־ דִּבְרֵי֙ נָתָ֣ן הַנָּבִ֔יא וְעַל־ נְבוּאַ֞ת אֲחִיָּ֣ה הַשִּֽׁילוֹנִ֗י וּבַחֲזוֹת֙ יֶעְדִּי הַחֹזֶ֔ה עַל־ יָרָבְעָ֖ם בֶּן־ נְבָֽט׃

passages.text: Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel forty years.
passages.sermon:
Solomon was king.
He ruled in Jerusalem.
He ruled over all Israel.
He ruled for forty years.
passages.original: וַיִּמְלֹ֨ךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֧ה בִֽירוּשָׁלִַ֛ם עַל־ כָּל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אַרְבָּעִ֥ים שָׁנָֽה׃

passages.text: And Solomon rested with his fathers and was buried in the city of his father David. And his son Rehoboam reigned in his place.
passages.sermon:
Solomon was king over all Israel.
Solomon died.
People buried Solomon in the city of David.
David was Solomon’s father.
Rehoboam was Solomon’s son.
Rehoboam became king after Solomon.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב שְׁלֹמֹה֙ עִם־ אֲבֹתָ֔יו וַֽיִּקְבְּרֻ֔הוּ בְּעִ֖יר דָּוִ֣יד אָבִ֑יו וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ רְחַבְעָ֥ם בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃פ
